chapter: Band building and learning from musicians
title: Teaching by band versus individual lessons
summary: Allen asks how to start the school; DeVore favors the band setting because of collective improvisation.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: involved in tonality though? If we're going to set up some sort of little school or something do you think how do you think we should start? Do you think we should start with individual lessons from an old musician to a young guy or should it be the band or what or both or everything? Well the way I see it

you'd have to the musicians that you'd have to start up on an individual basis it would be possible to take a man perhaps who didn't have any musical background or experience and just wanted to understand the philosophy that went into the music. That's one end. But from a strict playing end to me it always would seem that the most ideal setting would be a band setting because from a band angle I think a person can appreciate the give and take of New Orleans music much more than from an individual angle. To me the beauty of New Orleans music was collective improvisation and because of that I've always believed that the band is more important than the individual. The good of the band and the ability to be able to play with other men because you yourself know when you get a bunch of all stars together they could be just great individually in their instruments and really good men on their instruments from a jazz standpoint but they couldn't play together. It always meant more to me to be able to have it from a band angle so that's what I would say. And then to start out like I said before the chords the melody the trombone way of doing things and the clarinet way of doing things which I described earlier. And then I should explain this because a good band is a three rhythm or a three or four rhythm in the three front lines so you'd have the drumming and the bass. Now I didn't mention much about the drums before. For a drummer to start out we're taking everything this for granted that the men if you wanted a man to do something on his instrument he could do it because he had some previous background experience maybe not experience but a training on his instrument and that would hold true for all the men. all that taken for granted then you would start out with your band. And I mentioned the other instruments now a drumming that can be broken on quite simply too. Four four on the bass drum because that's the easiest to understand. Snare press rolls those two things. All a man would have to have is a bass drum and a snare drum. Where does he play the press roll? He plays the press rolls on two and four. Now a press roll I'm not a drummer myself I can't exactly explain it.
